overall: Los Angeles is seeing a mild, partly sunny morning with the running max reaching 66.2°F by mid-morning, warming at roughly +1.8°F/hr. South winds at ~10 mph are contributing a light marine influence, keeping conditions cooler than a typical late-June day. An active Air Quality Alert for windblown dust and a Wind Advisory for the nearby Mojave/Indian Wells areas suggest offshore pressure gradients are in play, though the LA coastal zone appears insulated from the strongest gusts.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement: ECMWF (71.2°F) and HRRR (71.6°F) are tightly clustered about 2-4°F above the NWS official forecast (69°F) and NBM (67.2°F), which lean more conservative and marine-influenced. The INTRADAY model appears to be extrapolating early warming rates too aggressively, producing a spurious spike near 84-85°F that is inconsistent with the NWP consensus and current synoptic setup.
max_temp_prediction: The META model — the most reliable signal — concentrates over 80% of probability in the 72-75°F band (40.9% at 74-75°F, 39.6% at 72-73°F), well-aligned with the ECMWF/HRRR cluster near 71-72°F. With the running max already at 66.2°F and several hours of warming still ahead, reaching the 69-72°F range is nearly certain; breaching 75°F would require faster warming than models anticipate. Best estimate is ~73.5°F, with moderate confidence — the ensemble abort signals and bucket spread suggest skipping active market bets today.
